assessment: All 11 retained main-PDF pages were read as text and visually inspected, including enlarged views of the five figures (18 panels) and small equations. All 33 numbered equations and 51 native bibliography entries were inspected. Two scoped checks against exact originals qualify the prior-work account. The 67 limited checks, nine transcribed country rows, 21 synthetic deployment rows and six synthetic LP cases do not reproduce native global C3IAM/GCOP. Explicit SI, data/code, 49 other originals and fourteen dependencies or audit requirements remain unverified. No public field dataset or accepted operating/GHG input was added.

sections.assessment: Yi-Ming Wei et al., Nature Climate Change 11 (2021), 112–118; DOI 10.1038/s41558-020-00960-0. Received 10 November 2019, accepted 2 November 2020, online 4 January 2021. Ten authors and affiliations read. The exclusive Springer licence is not assumed to be CC BY. Headline feasibility is conditional planning.

Read the global/regional data and method gaps, 94−2 Gt target, clustering and cost literature. Two selected originals support and qualify earlier integrated and continent-scale work; the other original chains remain unverified.

CARMA 2009 proportions are updated with 2017 IEA totals; 20,491 US/China/Europe points supplement 10 km EDGAR data downscaled through 1 km land-cover exclusions. Locations are fixed to 2050. The main-text 40,000 t/y and Methods 0.4 Mt/y thresholds remain unresolved.

Read the 180 oil and 614 saline basins, high-level US DOE volumetric method, geological scenarios and transnational area allocation. Offshore resource is included despite the onshore injection assumption. No pressure/time-conditioned basin service is demonstrated.
Read the 3,093 clusters, 432 sinks, 85 regions, 58.61/33.39 Gt split, distances and eight national maps/Sankey. Country, gross/capture and match-count/mass denominators remain distinct.

Read gross investment of USD 8.2 trillion, net cost 5.76 trillion, EOR benefit 2.44 trillion, unit cost 62.65 USD/t, country groups, GDP and oil-price indicators. Financial normalization is not emissions avoidance or causal GDP growth.

Read the 76% eight-country contribution, 21.54% average EOR utilization, geological ranges, ±20% cost and oil 55→95 sensitivity, financing recommendations and explicit geological/full-process cost limitations. Native cases remain missing.

All 51 numbered bibliography entries were read and their native lines/bboxes retained. R10 and R16 have scoped original-passage checks only; 49 other direct originals and fourteen dependencies or audit requirements remain unverified.

Equations 3–14 describe a cumulative domestic direct-arc cost/flow LP. Cross-border transport is prohibited; sector targets are lower bounds, capacities are stocks and flows are nonnegative. Mixed-source and cost/mass unit mappings remain open.

Equations 15–27 cover four technologies, annual installed capacity, a 52 Gt goal, terminal capacity/growth bounds, learning onsets, a 100 GW maturity assumption, component learning and LCOE-derived costs. Native inputs, paths and solver are missing.

Equations 28–33 describe deployment, learning, CEPCI and discounted annual costs for steel, cement, chemicals and BECCS. Threshold direction, cost versus deployment learning, sector/time mapping and initialization remain open.

Data and code are offered by the corresponding author upon reasonable request; page 11 points to DOI-linked SI. Funding, contributions, no competing interests and peer-review/reprint notices were read. No author was contacted and no matched local code or SI was verified.

equations.check: Uses 1.977 kg/m³ at standard conditions and E_oil=0.6. OOIP volume units, conditions and displaced-oil/replacement convention require the original/SI. Only a disclosed synthetic product is checked; no reservoir-density substitution.

equations.printed: V_CO2 = A × delta_A × h × phi × rho_CO2 × E
equations.check: A is area, delta_A an area fraction, h gross thickness, phi porosity, rho=710 kg/m³ and E=0.05. Their product is mass despite the V symbol. Gross/net thickness conventions and SI parameters remain open; pressure and time are absent.

equations.printed: min f = sum_pij[(CC_pi + TRC_pi,pj D_pi,pj + SC_pj)X_pi,pj] + sum_piq[(CC_pi + TRC_pi,pq D_pi,pq + SC_pq − Rev_pq)X_pi,pq]
equations.check: Cumulative linear cost with domestic direct arcs. TRC needs inverse-distance units when multiplied by D. No opening, shared network, annual capacity or pressure terms are printed. Synthetic negative EOR marginal costs can yield flows above minimum targets.
Emission-weighted cost requires capture-efficiency, flow and sector reconciliation for mixed clusters. This is not a complete heat/electricity inventory.
Gross cumulative emissions are additive; captured, injected and avoided mass do not automatically equal this quantity.

P_oil is USD/bbl; dpr is printed as 4 without a unit. It must have t/bbl units for Rev to be USD/t. Under that conditional interpretation, 55/4 applied to 33.39 Gt yields 0.4591125 trillion USD, rather than 2.44 trillion. Native units, revenue, time and case basis remain unresolved; no correction inferred.

equations.printed: sum_j X_pi,pj + sum_q X_pi,pq <= eta1 E_pi, i in1..k
equations.check: A capture-efficiency bound, despite prose describing pipeline capacity. No separate arc capacity appears. E_total and mixed-sector attribution remain unresolved.

equations.printed: sum_j X_pi,pj + sum_q X_pi,pq <= eta2 E_pi, i ink+1..n
equations.check: Analogous nonpower capture-efficiency bound. Separate sector flows within mixed clusters are not shown.

equations.printed: sum_p sum_i=1..k sum_j X_pi,pj + sum_p sum_i=1..k sum_q X_pi,pq >= RRC_powerA
equations.check: A 52 Gt lower-bound capture target; exact equality is not forced under all costs. This is not a whole-chain avoided-GHG functional unit.

equations.printed: sum_p sum_i=k+1..n sum_j X_pi,pj + sum_p sum_i=k+1..n sum_q X_pi,pq >= RRC_nonpowerA
equations.check: A 40 Gt lower bound. The synthetic exact-target comparison is an explicitly different diagnostic constraint, not a correction of native code.
A per-sink cumulative stock bound, rather than annual injectivity or the country aggregate described in surrounding prose.
EOR cumulative stock bound; not permanent retained mass or an incremental-oil climate credit.
Nonnegative cumulative saline flow. Feasibility requires native source/sink inputs.
Nonnegative cumulative EOR flow. There is no independent equality fixing global flow at 92 Gt.

equations.printed: min TCC_elec = sum_t=2020..2050 sum_s=1..4 [CC_s(t) Cum_s(t) H CF_s (ER_s,ref − ER_s,CCS) (1+r)^−(t−2020)]
equations.check: The sum includes 31 calendar entries. Capacity × hours × capacity factor × emission-rate difference is avoided CO2 at equal output. Mapping to captured mass and the native learning path is missing; the discount rate is in unverified SI.
The positive-domain learning component is checked using b=log2(1−LR). Zero-capacity initialization, learning onset and the 100 GW maturity branches remain unverified.

equations.printed: sum_t=2020..2050 sum_s Cum_s(t) H CF_s (ER_s,ref − ER_s,CCS) >= RRC_powerA
equations.check: The 52 Gt constraint uses an avoided-emission-rate difference. Its mapping to the network captured-mass target is unverified; no annual deployment output is supplied.
A maximum 2050 thermal capacity; parameter values and capacity-unit conversions remain unverified in SI/originals.
The printed nonnegative growth rule precludes retirement in this capacity path. Initial capacity, horizon-boundary indexing and growth limits remain missing.
Fixed initial capital-share weighted component learning. Weights must sum to one; all native component costs/rates are needed.
Analogous O&M share weighting. Annual cost basis and fuel allocation remain separate.

equations.printed: LCOE = (CRF sum_w I_w + sum_w C_w,OM + C_fuel)/(CF H P)
equations.check: Annualized capital plus annual O&M/fuel divided by annual electricity. The Eq24 identity is reconstructed only with disclosed analyst costs and capacity factors.

Cost per avoided tonne at matched electricity output, not automatically per captured tonne. A synthetic 40 USD/MWh difference divided by 0.7 t avoided/MWh gives 57.1429 USD/t; a separate 0.8 t captured/MWh gives 50 USD/t.
The CF_0/CF_d factor was verified enlarged. Direct annualized LCOE and the expansion agree under analyst assumptions with fixed P/H/CRF; no native coefficients were invented.
COE/LCOE notation varies. Equality requires a common emission-rate difference and consistent output/capacity conventions. It does not supply all energy or process capture quantities.
Requires nonzero initial CC and a consistent avoided-mass basis. LCOE learning alone does not establish all capture-cost components.
Discounted capture cost is divided by the 52 Gt target. This is an average cost parameter, not a source-specific matched utility inventory.

The literal rising exponential-of-squared-distance segment is checked. At SD it is tp_max exp(−U²), and at 2050 it is tp_max. It is not the standard logistic equation. U must be dimensionless; native SD/U/maximum remain missing.

CR=0.25. The printed condition tp>CR_min contrasts with prose saying below the threshold. The equation reduces a cost multiplier while prose also describes deployment reduction. Initial and otherwise branches remain missing; no silent repair.
Initial cost × learning multiplier × price index. CEPCI base normalization, sector values and timing remain unverified in SI.
CAP captured mass must match the annual cost period. CAP(t) and its link to tp(t) are not explicit. BECCS allocation outside the three original industrial grid classes needs native data.
Initial year, calendar convention, discount rate and annual CAP mapping remain missing. The native nonpower deployment is not reproduced.

The average divides by the 40 Gt target. Surrounding prose calls this the power cluster, an unresolved copy-label question. No complete heat/electricity/compression/liquefaction/cooling inventory follows.

variables.name: Emission grids, clusters and thresholds
variables.assumption: Cells exceed 10,000 t/y. Body says clusters exceed 40,000 t/y; Methods says 0.4 Mt/y. The 2017 location pattern is held fixed.

variables.name: CARMA, EDGAR and MODIS coordinates
variables.assumption: Output resolution is not measurement accuracy. Land-cover exclusions include forest, wetlands, snow/ice and water.

variables.name: G_CO2, OOIP, standard density and E_oil
variables.unit: mass; oil-volume unit unstated; 1.977 kg/m³; fraction 0.6
variables.assumption: Oil/standard-volume replacement and formation-volume conventions remain unresolved.

variables.name: V_CO2, A, delta_A, h, phi, rho and E
variables.unit: mass; m²; fraction; m; fraction; 710 kg/m³; fraction 0.05
variables.assumption: Volumetric resource. Gross/net thickness and porosity choices require SI. No pressure or duration limit follows.

variables.name: p, i, j, q, k, n, m, z and l
variables.assumption: Cross-border arcs are prohibited. Mixed clusters need explicit sector allocation.

variables.name: X, Q and E
variables.unit: consistently scaled cumulative t or Gt
variables.assumption: Transport/capture flows, sink stocks and gross emissions are different variables. No annual rate is implicit.

variables.name: CC, SC, TRC and D
variables.unit: USD/t; USD/t; USD/(t km) required; km
variables.assumption: Direct arc distance and cost. Route, shared-network and hydraulic capacity are not independently specified.

variables.name: P_oil, dpr and Rev
variables.unit: base 55 USD/bbl; printed 4 without unit; USD/t required
variables.assumption: t/bbl is a conditional dimensional interpretation only. Revenue is not a GHG credit.

variables.name: eta1, eta2 and RRC sector targets
variables.unit: fractions; 52 Gt power and 40 Gt nonpower
variables.assumption: Capture efficiencies are not inferred. Printed target constraints are lower bounds.

variables.name: TCC and sector-average CC
variables.assumption: Constant 2019 prices are reported. The discount rate and native averaging mapping require SI.

variables.name: Cum_s, H, CF and ER
variables.unit: MW/GW with conversion; h/y; fraction; t/MWh
variables.assumption: Capacity and electricity units must agree. The ER difference represents avoided emissions at equal output.

variables.name: S_max, A_max and technology sets
variables.assumption: Initial capacity, growth, maturity at 100 GW and 2020/2030 onset settings require native implementation.

variables.name: a_s, b_s, lambda, alpha and LR
variables.unit: cost/capacity-exponent coefficient; dimensionless exponents, weights and fractions
variables.assumption: Positive-capacity learning and fixed initial cost shares; native fitting is not reproduced.

variables.name: I, C_OM, C_fuel, CRF, P and LCOE
variables.assumption: Annualization, capacity factor and equal-output counterfactual must be consistent.

variables.name: Initial 0 and doubled-capacity d subscripts
variables.assumption: They are not stochastic draws. Eq25 assumes common ER values; Eq24 retains the capacity-factor change.

variables.name: tp, U, SD and tp_max
variables.assumption: The rising segment is used only from SD to 2050. Deployment at SD is generally nonzero.

variables.name: lc, CR and CR_min
variables.assumption: The printed greater-than condition contrasts with prose saying below. Cost and deployment reduction meanings remain open.

variables.name: CI, CEPCI, ec, CAP and C_nele
variables.unit: USD/t; index; USD/t; t/y needed; USD/y
variables.assumption: Index base, annual CAP and deployment link remain missing. BECCS sector mapping is not supplied.

variables.name: Cost, benefit, GDP and oil breakeven
variables.assumption: Cost minus revenue is not causal GDP output or climate benefit. Native price/discount/case bases remain open.

variables.name: Match distances, counts and volume
variables.assumption: Mass and count percentages are not interchangeable. Short distance alone does not demonstrate feasibility.

variables.name: Geological and cost scenarios
variables.unit: 124–300 Gt EOR; 888–5,126 Gt saline; ±20% cost; oil 55→95 USD/bbl
variables.assumption: Scenario envelopes are not calibrated probabilities or annual pressure/retention uncertainty.

claims.claim: CCUS contributes 92 Gt mitigation consistent with a 2°C target.
claims.assessment: The 94−2 Gt IEA target is source accounting, not independent climate-scenario or whole-chain avoided-mass verification.

claims.claim: Development is below 1% of projected capture and concentrated in few countries.
claims.assessment: A historical author claim; the IEA originals remain unverified and this is not a current project inventory.

claims.claim: Earlier work mostly concerns cost, transport and local matching; a global gap remains.
claims.assessment: The selected SimCCS original already integrates capture, storage and routes, qualifying a narrow transport-only description. InfraCCS supports continent-scale temporal precedent. Exhaustive novelty is not verified.

claims.claim: Clusters reduce costs and risks and share infrastructure.
claims.assessment: A planning argument, rather than measured reliability or proof that this LP implements shared trunk networks.

claims.claim: A unified global database supports high-resolution storage assessment.
claims.assessment: Downscaling and volumetric methods do not establish observed 1 km geology or field injectivity.

claims.claim: There are 4,220 clusters in 87 countries under the stated definition.
claims.assessment: The count is not regenerated; 40,000 t/y in the body and 0.4 Mt/y in Methods differ tenfold.

claims.claim: The global source database integrates CARMA and nonpower information.
claims.assessment: 66,273 power points from 2009 are scaled to 2017 IEA totals; 20,491 US/China/Europe industrial points complement downscaled EDGAR. Versions and accuracy are not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: Physical cluster locations will not change markedly within thirty years.
claims.assessment: An exogenous persistence assumption excluding force majeure, not an actual retirement/new-build forecast.

claims.claim: The clusters emit 693.8 Gt cumulatively, including 518.8 Gt power emissions.
claims.assessment: Power accounts for about 74.78%; native annual spatial arrays remain unavailable.

claims.claim: Cluster counts are 47% mixed, 24% power-only and 29% nonpower-only.
claims.assessment: Shares sum to 100%; the mixed-cluster sector-flow mapping in Eq7–10 remains open.

claims.claim: 90% of clusters exceed 0.1 Gt cumulative emissions; 47 countries are almost all power.
claims.assessment: Reported population claims require native arrays; they cannot be reconstructed from the map alone.

claims.claim: Eight inventory regions contribute about 81% of cluster counts and 84% of emissions.
claims.assessment: Their Fig1 masses imply 81.565% of emissions. Display rounding alone does not reach 84% if the case/denominator is the same. Count and mass are not swapped or corrected.

claims.claim: Fig1 reports regional cumulative masses and power/industry shares.
claims.assessment: Nine masses sum to 693.6 versus 693.8 Gt globally; rounded pie weights imply 517.608 versus 518.8 Gt power. Both differences are compatible with the display precision.

claims.claim: 794 basins have 2,082 Gt effective storage resource.
claims.assessment: 180 EOR/614 saline basins and 168/1,914 Gt add correctly. These are cumulative resources without annual pressure or containment constraints.

claims.claim: US DOE and CSLF methods are essentially equivalent for high-level assessment.
claims.assessment: Underlying methods remain unverified; the authors explicitly select national/basin-scale estimation because detailed global geology is unavailable.

claims.claim: EOR resource includes known miscible or near-miscible oil fields.
claims.assessment: Undiscovered and unconventional high-pressure/high-sulfur reservoirs are excluded. Full field EOS, recycling, leakage and economic cases are not reproduced.

claims.claim: Saudi Arabia, Russia and Iraq have 17.9%, 17% and 12% of EOR potential; the top ten have 78.2%.
claims.assessment: Reported allocation shares; native per-basin resource is not independently validated.

claims.claim: Russia exceeds 12%, Australia has about 10% and Brazil 7% of saline potential; the top ten have 65.3%.
claims.assessment: Reported area-based national allocations, not territorial storage-service contracts.

claims.claim: Only onshore injection is considered but offshore basin resource extent is included.
claims.assessment: An explicit caption boundary requiring spatial, cost and accessible-mass reconciliation before transfer.

claims.claim: Transnational basin resources are allocated by area.
claims.assessment: This differs from the majority-country whole-basin assignment in B2-15. National differences cannot be attributed solely to pressure constraints.

claims.claim: 3,093 clusters, 432 sinks and 85 regions are selected.
claims.assessment: These are 73.29%, 54.41% and 97.70% of the corresponding input populations. Selection is not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: 58.61 Gt goes to saline storage and 33.39 Gt to EOR.
claims.assessment: They sum to 92 Gt, or 63.71%/36.29%; 277+155 selected sinks sum to 432. Whole-chain avoided or permanently retained mass is unverified.

claims.claim: Saline flow is about half power; EOR flow is 66% power.
claims.assessment: The latter implies about 22.0374 Gt using the rounded share. Exact sector/sink quantities require SI Table 1.

claims.claim: 80% of matches are within 300 km and none exceeds 1,000 km.
claims.assessment: Figure caption match counts and national mass percentages need their own denominators. Short arc distance is not field feasibility.

claims.claim: Eight selected regions contain 2,399 clusters/197 sinks and undertake 76% of target mass.
claims.assessment: Rounded Fig4 masses sum to 69.8 Gt, or 75.87% of 92. This selected-country set differs from Fig1’s eight inventory regions.

claims.claim: More than 91% of mass is within 300 km in the USA, EU, Australia and Saudi Arabia.
claims.assessment: A reported scenario result, not a ship-network, pipeline-hydraulic or storage-capacity validation.

claims.claim: India/Mexico have 70–80% within 300 km; China/Russia have >11%/>17% beyond 500 km.
claims.assessment: Native distance/flow arrays remain missing. Precise routes are not inferred from circles.

claims.claim: China selects 66% of 1,430 clusters for 26.68 Gt, 72% nonpower, about one-fifth EOR.
claims.assessment: These are rounded proportions; 944 is not asserted as an exact selected count. Native allocation remains unverified.

claims.claim: The USA selects 58% of 841 clusters for 16.09 Gt, 63% power and 5.27 Gt EOR.
claims.assessment: The EOR mass ratio is 32.753%; 488 is not asserted as an exact selected count. Native allocation remains unverified.

claims.claim: The EU captures 8.97 Gt from 507 clusters and India 3.80 Gt from 163; saline exceeds 75%.
claims.assessment: Reported country cases, rather than validated individual sources or annual storage service.

claims.claim: Russia/Saudi Arabia/Mexico mainly use EOR; Australia captures 1.86 Gt, 98% power.
claims.assessment: Reported case and cost context; the Australian rounded power share implies 1.8228 Gt.

claims.claim: Gross investment is USD 8.20 trillion; net cost is 5.76 trillion and 62.65 USD/t.
claims.assessment: Component/net identities and unit-cost rounding reconcile. Financial cost does not establish net emissions.

claims.claim: Capture costs USD 4.45 trillion, more than 77% of total cost.
claims.assessment: This is 77.26% of net cost but 54.27% of gross investment. The net denominator explains the statement; it is not an arithmetic error.

claims.claim: Power/nonpower account for 61%/39% of capture costs; transport/storage cost 3.25/0.50 trillion USD.
claims.assessment: Cost shares are not utility inventories or full LCA. Native learning and flow/cost mappings remain unverified.

claims.claim: EOR provides USD 2.44 trillion of benefits.
claims.assessment: Under the explicitly conditional interpretation dpr=4 t/bbl, Eq6 with 55 USD/bbl and 33.39 Gt gives 0.459 trillion. Units, revenue and case/time basis need reconciliation; no corrected benefit is adopted.

claims.claim: Four countries earn USD 2.49 million to 4.66 billion while 81 pay costs.
claims.assessment: National financial net is not net GHG. Native country profit and cost arrays remain missing.

claims.claim: China/USA/EU cost about 2.01/0.94/0.58 trillion USD; page 7 gives maximum 2.02 trillion.
claims.assessment: Adjacent 0.01-trillion display intervals touch, so a definite 2.01/2.02 error is not claimed. The USA value is not replaced with an axis tick.

claims.claim: Groups I/II/III/IV contain 3/10/64/8 regions; reported mass shares include 3.7%, 79% and 10%.
claims.assessment: Group II count and Group IV’s approximately 7.3% mass remainder are analyst arithmetic, not new native data.

claims.claim: National unit costs range from −10.02 to 125.06 USD/t.
claims.assessment: Financial net per source mass, not whole-chain avoidance cost. The text pointer to Fig5b corresponds to panel c.

claims.claim: Total cost is about 0.12% of cumulative GDP and economically feasible.
claims.assessment: Rounded values imply about USD 4,800 trillion cumulative GDP. This is not an annual budget or proof of each country’s ability to finance upfront costs.

claims.claim: Four countries increase GDP by 0.0002–0.05%.
claims.assessment: The displayed calculation normalizes financial surplus by exogenous SSP2 GDP; an endogenous causal growth model is not demonstrated.

claims.claim: Russia/China/Saudi Arabia/USA/EU costs are 0.36/0.18/0.17/0.14/0.11% of GDP.
claims.assessment: Reported country ratios; native SSP, price-year and discounting bases remain unverified.

claims.claim: Breakeven oil prices span 34.51–330.39 USD/bbl, mean 134.58; 25 profit at 75 and 75% above 100.
claims.assessment: A skewed distribution can reconcile the high mean and a majority below 100. Native eligible population and weighting are needed; no false contradiction is asserted.

claims.claim: Global average EOR potential utilization is 21.54%.
claims.assessment: Aggregate flow/resource is 19.875%. An unweighted country average could differ. The basis is unresolved, rather than declared erroneous.

claims.claim: New emitters near EOR and more utilization technologies could offset costs.
claims.assessment: Policy recommendations under a conditional financial model, not assessed climate benefit, permission or deployment.

claims.claim: Geological scenarios give 124–300 Gt EOR and 888–5,126 Gt saline resources.
claims.assessment: Input scenario envelopes, not calibrated probabilities or annual pressure/retention uncertainty.

claims.claim: A 20% initial cost increase gives 7.38 trillion USD, 80.26 USD/t and 30.84 Gt EOR.
claims.assessment: 80.26×92 Gt implies 7.38392 trillion, compatible with rounding. Reoptimization is not a linear 20% net-cost response.

claims.claim: A 20% initial cost decrease gives 4.13 trillion USD, a 17.77 USD/t saving and 33.36 Gt EOR.
claims.assessment: 62.65−17.77=44.88 USD/t implies 4.12896 trillion at 92 Gt, compatible with rounding. Native cases remain unverified.

claims.claim: Oil price 55→95 USD/bbl reduces unit cost to 40.26 USD/t and shifts EOR countries.
claims.assessment: At the same 92 Gt this implies 3.70392 trillion USD. Fixed-volume Eq6 calculations do not reproduce the reoptimized case.

claims.claim: Geological and full-process cost differences are ignored; future technology changes results.
claims.assessment: An explicit high-level limitation; financing/technology-transfer recommendations remain conditional.

claims.claim: C3IAM/GCOP minimizes capture, transport and storage cost.
claims.assessment: The printed model is a cumulative domestic direct-arc LP, not annual network construction, hydraulics or field dispatch.

claims.claim: Source capture is bounded by pipeline capacity.
claims.assessment: Printed eta×E bounds efficiency-weighted source emissions, without separate arc capacity. Native SI/code may contain unreported conditions.

claims.claim: Power/nonpower capture requirements are 52/40 Gt.
claims.assessment: Printed lower bounds do not guarantee exact equality. Negative marginal EOR costs produce extra capture in synthetic cases, without proving a native-case error.

claims.claim: Four power capture technologies have endogenous learning and capacity constraints.
claims.assessment: IGCCC/SPCC/NGCCC/Oxy inputs, initialization, onset/maturity and growth settings remain missing. Eq16 is singular at zero for a negative learning exponent.

claims.claim: LCOE learning determines capture cost.
